answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent's reputation to a verifiable stake of earned work history rather than to free accounts: a new identity starts with zero trust and must complete small, paid, audited tasks before it can transact at scale. Each fake identity then costs real time and fees, so the ripple of cheap clones collapses - the delta between the cost of one fake and the value it can extract stays negative, making mass fakery unprofitable.
